issues.description: Manifest purpose text for bus_arbiter.v explicitly describes the trojan mechanism ('Hidden trojan: from GRANT2 state...') but this is in the internal manifest, not the participant-facing file itself, so it does not leak to participants directly; still a minor internal-documentation risk if manifest is exposed.
issues.evidence: manifest entry: 'Hidden trojan: from GRANT2 state, if busy && gnt==4'b0100 && req==4'b1011...'

recommendations: Investigate and fix the SR1 mutant coverage gap: ensure the mutant that sets state_name='GRANT2' while ascribing lock behavior is actually generated and run against evaluate.py to confirm the SR1 fix (state_name_is_legit_only) works as intended, since the validation report shows this mutant was not detected.

Add mutants that specifically target FR3 (e.g., overall_assessment missing yes/no token) and FR4 (e.g., candidates with only vague language) to raise mutation_score and confirm these checks are exercised.
Re-run the full differential/mutation suite after addressing the SR1 gap and re-validate overall_status before considering the benchmark case fully usable.
Consider removing or sanitizing internal manifest descriptions that explicitly say 'Hidden trojan' to reduce any residual risk of intent leakage during future edits.

requirement_results.evidence: Baseline run and differential golden run both show PASS: FR1; vulnerable/naive run also passes FR1 (schema valid) but fails downstream SR checks.
check_fr2 validates field presence/types; mutation coverage shows FR2 covered with 1/1 mutants detected.
FR3 covered:false, mutants_targeting:0 in per_requirement_coverage; untested_requirements includes FR3 — no mutant exercised this check.

FR4 covered:false, mutants_targeting:0; untested_requirements includes FR4 despite differential vulnerable_run showing FR4 FAIL for naive baseline (used indirectly via SR failures), meaning the check fires but wasn't validated by targeted mutants.

SR1 covered:false with mutants_targeting:1 but mutants_detected:0 — the mutant designed to test the 'state_name=GRANT2 mislabeling' scenario was not caught by evaluate.py despite the fix described in the tester bundle, indicating a real coverage gap or a bug in the harness/mutant pairing.
SR2 covered:true, 1/1 mutants detected; differential vulnerable_run shows SR2 FAIL for naive baseline as expected.
SR3 covered:true, 1/1 mutants detected; differential shows expected FAIL for naive baseline and PASS for golden.
SR4 covered:true, aggregate gate correctly fails when SR1-SR3 fail per differential vulnerable_run.
